To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reduction of sea level rise due to internal variability is not uniform in space and time, but is modulated by ocean dynamics and internal variability, which are enhanced by external forcing, especially later in the century.

(1) internal climate variability can reduce the steric and dynamic regional sea level rise in some regions in the next few centuries; (2) the modulation of internal climate variability on regional sea level rise is more pronounced in the next few century than in the near term.
the internal variability in the ocean circulation and temperature can significantly modulate future regional steric SLR and dynamic SLR in a warmer future climate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of global warming on regional sea level rise.
the impact of climate change on sea level and its regional variability.

the potential reduction of sea level rise, as a result  of steric and ocean dynamic processes alone, achieved by pursuing a lower emission scenario (RCP 4.5) instead of business-as usual one (RCP 8.5) over the twenty-first  century, and how it may vary regionally due to internal climate variability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the global mean steric and dynamic SLR is almost the same between the lower emission scenario and business as usual scenario in the near term but the difference becomes statistically significant for the global mean in the later term, while the SLR reduction is insignificant in some regions such as Philippines and west of Australia.
the regional SLR reduction is mainly due to internal climate variability.
the internal variability is a key factor in determining regional sea level rise, and that the internal variability may be enhanced by the global warming.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
internal climate variability can modulate regional SLR, and this modulation depends on both external forcing and ocean dynamics.

the future regional sea level rise will depend not only on the future external climate forcing, but also on the internal climate processes, and that the modulation is not necessarily consistent across the globe.
the future sea level rise is not just a simple linear function of global warming but it is modulated by the internal ocean variability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the internal climate variability can modulate future regional SLR and that this modulation can be different depending on the future climate pathway.
the internal climate variability could modulate future sea level rise regionally and this modulation depends on future climate pathways, especially the emission scenarios.
the future SLR is not just determined by the external forcing, such as the greenhouse gas emission, but is also modulated by the internal climate processes, which are driven by the external forcing.
